market_context: United States and Canada; household towel care focused on load size, detergent, absorbency, full drying, and odor prevention.
title: How to Wash Towels Properly

seo.title: How to Wash Towels So They Stay Clean and Absorbent
seo.meta_description: Give towels room in the washer, measure detergent, go easy on fabric softener, and dry them completely to prevent residue and musty odor.
seo.search_intent: Wash and dry towels while maintaining cleanliness and absorbency without detergent buildup or lingering moisture.

excerpt: To wash towels properly, sort by color, leave room in the drum, measure detergent, and follow the care label for water temperature. If towels lose absorbency, reduce fabric softener. Dry them completely after washing and hang them open between uses so they do not stay damp.
content_html:
A towel can smell clean out of the washer and still become stiff, less absorbent, or musty after only a few uses. Good towel care is less about adding extra products and more about allowing enough washing, rinsing, and complete drying.

A dependable routine is to avoid overloading, measure detergent, follow the care label, and make sure towels are fully dry before storage.

Sort by color and soil level

New dark or brightly colored towels may release dye during early washes. Keep whites with whites and darker colors with similar items.

Pre-treat makeup, mud, or heavy body-product stains rather than increasing detergent for the entire load.

Give towels room in the washer

Towels absorb a lot of water and become heavy. If they are packed tightly, wash water and rinse water cannot move through the load as effectively.

If a finished load feels soapy or smells stale, try fewer towels next time.

Measure detergent instead of guessing

Too much detergent can remain in dense loops and make towels feel harsh. Use the amount recommended for load size, soil level, water hardness, and your type of washer.

High-efficiency machines should use HE detergent when the manufacturer requires it.

Use the care label to choose water temperature

Many cotton towels tolerate warm water, while some white towels allow hotter settings. Dark colors may hold their appearance better at cooler temperatures.

The highest setting on the washer is not automatically the best setting for every towel.

Fabric softener can change absorbency

Softeners coat fibers to alter feel. With some towels, frequent use can reduce how readily the fabric absorbs water.

If towels begin to feel slick or stop drying effectively, skip softener for several washes and see whether performance improves.

Musty odor often starts between uses

The American Cleaning Institute recommends hanging bath towels to dry between uses and washing them after about three to five normal uses.

Do not leave a wet towel balled up on the floor or folded over itself where the center stays damp.

Dry completely after washing

Move towels out of the washer promptly. Use the care-label dryer setting and avoid running heat long after the load is dry.

If line drying, spread towels where air can reach them. Thick fabric can feel dry on the surface while remaining damp inside.

New towels may shed lint

Some lint release is normal during the first few washes. Clean the dryer lint screen as required and avoid washing brand-new towels with items that attract lint easily.

Excessive fiber loss, loose seams, or bare patches are a different issue and may indicate wear or a product defect.

Can towels be washed with regular clothes?

They can when color, temperature, and care needs match, but towels shed lint and their textured loops create more friction than many lightweight garments. Separate towel loads are often easier to rinse and keep lint away from delicate clothing.

A more uniform heavy load can also balance better than mixing one large towel with a handful of light items.

Every normal towel load does not need to be disinfected

For routine household use, effective washing with detergent followed by complete drying is usually the goal. Illness, body-fluid contamination, or a specific hygiene situation may call for different instructions.

In those cases, follow appropriate health guidance and the textile care label rather than adding stronger chemicals to every load.

If a clean towel smells after one use, look at how it dries

A towel folded over a narrow hook or crowded in a humid bathroom can stay damp in the middle for hours. That can create odor even when the laundry process was fine.

Spread it more fully and improve bathroom ventilation before changing detergent.

If towels stay stiff

Hard water and detergent residue can contribute. Recheck product dose and make sure the washer is rinsing effectively.

A clean towel does not need an intense fragrance or an artificially slippery feel. It should rinse clean, absorb water well, and dry fully before the next use.

faq.question: How often should bath towels be washed?
faq.answer: The American Cleaning Institute suggests washing after about three to five normal uses and allowing towels to dry between uses.

faq.question: Why are my towels less absorbent?
faq.answer: Fabric softener or detergent buildup can contribute. Reduce product use and make sure towels rinse thoroughly.

faq.question: Should towels be washed in hot water?
faq.answer: Follow the care label. Some towels tolerate hot water, but color and fabric construction may call for warm or cool settings.

faq.question: Why do towels smell musty?
faq.answer: They often stay damp too long in the washer, on a hook, or in storage before fully drying.
